reviews.text: Amazing how I managed to spend 36 hours on just the demo! The gameplay is an addictive mix of card roguelike, strategy, and that old Windows pipe connection game - sounds weird but it works perfectly. Now with the full release, I can't wait to explore all the additional content. Definitely recommend!

This game is actually really addicting and fun, I didn't think I would like it much due to the setting but it's charm and characters really turned it around for me. The gameplay seems simple at first but evolves really quickly, on my first run I thought it was too easy at first until suddenly they were throwing things at me I never thought of and before I knew it I could see possibilities that I could implement myself and that was awesome! Great!

Honneslty every run feels the exact same, the deck building aspect is very limited, with low opportunities to fine tune your deck and the board deck always being present anyway. It's mostly a grind to advance the story more than anything else. The game in itself is fine, the gameplay mechanics are fun and all but not much replayability...

The most frustrating thing, that made me write this review is that I have won 3 or 4 runs now, only to be met with a door that stops you from progressing until you've sat through enough of the story. That feels like I'm being punished for being good at the game and just artificially inflating the game length. And that padding is a lot too, I seem to be able to get at best 5% of the required story progression per run, this is a major buzzkill (much MUCH worse than the game being too short) and the primary reason I have uninstalled. the actual game-play is alright, it's an interesting concept. Every run feels pretty same-y, the cards you pick up don't really change your run to run playstyle. The story is very annoying but skippable. I also found there were many times where the outcome of the battle was obvious, but I still had to play out for a while. The AI is pretty dumb and very frequently does stuff that helps you out. I had a boss use a power to make my bases closer together and then installed a bunch of tesla coils around them making them a basically impenetrable fortress. Some of the bosses have powers that just deal damage to your base with no recourse, which isn't really great and makes it nearly impossible to strive for a perfect run or anything.

Fun concept, but quickly becomes repetitive and boring. It's lacking in content. What's even worse, is that the last (and presumably most difficult) area is locked behind "story progress". You progress the story buy entering story nodes when choosing a path on the overmap. It requires MANY runs to unlock enough story to enter the last campaign area. So, if you find the game too easy already, you have to grind over and over just to make it more difficult? And it's obviously worse by the aforementioned lack of content. It's a baffling design decision for a deck builder roguelike. For a roguelike, the game focuses a lot on telling a story, and there are a lot of voiced cutscenes. I haven't unlocked that much, but it all feels very "meh". It just presents minor variations on the same tropes. Wish the writing and characters were more interesting. As for style, think forgettable 2000s CN/Adult swim animation series that's only entertaining to kids (or stoners). The game isn't bad. The concept is well executed, I'd say. Good production value. It is however way overpriced for the content it delivers, and it doesn't have what it takes to stand out in such a saturated genre. I'd recommend if it were half the price, so pick it up on a deep sale.

A promising idea that quickly wears out its welcome. The "crazy game show" aesthetic reminds me of Dicey Dungeons, and the animation is done in a Teletoons-looking style. But the story is also a major flaw: the only way to play the true ending is to watch all 50+ cut scenes. Which are way too many for a story this simple (game show is run by crazy guy who's obviously the final boss). This forces players to choose the "story" path every time, taking away what should be an important game decision. The head-to-head train-track puzzle-solving gameplay is clever, but it felt like I was always ending my turn 5 moves early because I just didn't have any useful plays. And it seems like there's no real way to prevent damage to your base, especially from bombs the opponent can just place as desired. The "choose a contestant" mechanism works well, but their starting boosts are all over the place, making it hard to discover what works and what doesn't. It gets random and repetitive quickly. A multiplayer mode could be fun, though.

A very fun puzzle, deck building game. With a charming and fully dubbed story. Game also let you quit and resume from any point in the game, so it is easy to stop at any time. I had extremely fun playing this game and I highly recommend it.

i am of two minds about battle train. i REALLY love the concept and gameplay. it is really enjoyable to connect tracks against an opponent and the puzzle solving that comes with it. unfortunately, i would call just about everything else about it half-baked. somehow, it is still really fun in spite of that. i honestly only bought into this game now instead of during a deep sale because i was seeing the low turnout and lukewarm reviews and i wanted to support the team and i knew i'd enjoy playing it. i think the heart of the issue is that roguelike deckbuilder is a genre that ever since its grandfather Slay The Spire it has always been very tightly designed with frequent creatively designed risks and trade offs built into each encounter. battle train is clearly very deliberately loose in its design. it chooses style over substance and that's a shame for such a substantive foundation, but design like allowing bosses to directly hit you regardless of defense is neither intuitive nor properly curbed by surrounding mechanics. neither are the often lopsided maps. i've learned to be fine with that. the core of battle train is not in its fairness--it's a very beatable game even despite how unfair it feels at its worst--it really is the style. you have to love the game's abundance of story cutscenes at least a little bit, and appreciate how the game's story elements evolve every time you lap it. i cannot shake the feeling that battle train is a case of lost potential but i also sincerely have found it to be worth every penny just because of how incredibly addicting the base mechanics of building your track is.

7/10 It's hard to recommend the game and not recommend the game. It's fun and it's a different take on the roguelike deckbuilder, sure it may not have the depth and complexity of the more popular titles in the genre it's different. What makes the game hard to recommend is: 1) there is overarching story, your progress is hardlocked (you can't access the final map) until the you unlocked and reached certain story points in the game through multiple runs, regardless of how well you played or until the completed the entire story arc. 2) the game has a heavy RNG element, you are at the whims of RNG on what your selection of starting characters are and what cards and items you come across in any given run. You don't really have control of doing or trying a specific build or strategy, only that you've picked the best possible choice of rewards/items along your way. Check out the global stat for % of some achievements, there's a reason why a lot just can't be bothered. 3) like most roguelike deckbuilders, you get branching paths to choose what you encounter and what order during your map run, sadly the differences in between the paths is so minuscule that's going to hardly make a difference. What could have been done better in my opinion: 1) offer at least some substitute for the final map, even if the official final map in a run doesn't get unlocked during said moments of the story. 2) offer gold or at least some form of consolation reward if the none of the rewards from completing an encounter doesn't offer anything useful 3) offer a balanced selection, cards geared toward a specific build as well as generic during encounter rewards and shops. In shops at least offer 5 commons, 3 uncommons and 2 rares cards or something and guaranteed variety of train parts and accessories. For instance 3 different train parts guaranteed and 2 accessories. It's a bummer when you reach a shop and all it sells are options for the only type of train part you've upgraded. 4) more specific choice of starting set of cards and accessories. Sometimes if feels you're choosing the less detrimental of the 3 starting characters rather than excited with analysis paralysis which one you want to run with. 5) Game should offer a fixed amount of healing post each boss fight. It's almost dubious for the designers to expect you to complete each boss fight unscathed, especially considering how unfairly tuned some are and cards that do unpreventable direct damage. The limited option to repair your train damage is so bizarre, considering a lot of fights boils down to you trading blows with your opponent in damage, you have no option to repair your train above the damage it started a battle with even though it's below max and once your outpost is destroyed it can't be repaired. Yet there's an achievement that asks you complete an entire run finishing with no damage. It's a fun game, and it might even get you hooked but you need to realize that your folly of how successful/fun each run is dependent on 1) whether you've progressed the story enough 2) RNG.
This game was crafted in a lab to appeal specifically to me.

I really wanted to love this game... but it just isn't all that fun, then as if the dev knew that there wasn't enough content and it wasn't that good, they lock gameplay behind a story gate which just forces grinding. I would recommend to the dev that they should spend less time on 'backstage' cut scenes and more time on the gameplay and mini games. Also, instead of cards maybe a 'roll and write' style of gameplay could be fun? Where you customize and upgrade the dice you roll for your abilities/track. This got grindy REAL fast. Imagine if Enter the Gungeon/binding of Issac/Dead souls stopped you at the 3rd level and 'gamed over' your run because you haven't gotten to the 3rd floor 6 times already? It's just makes you feel bad as player. This could be worth 3-5 bucks, but even then I would probably not play just because of forcing a run loss because you need to beat the game 5+ times before getting more game.

FUN game but some major design issues. Good first: This game is actually a lot of fun, the puzzle piece design of tracks is an interesting mechanic, and its always satisfying to actually fill up space the most efficient way while also blocking your own stuff while also reaching into enemy territory but not too much at the same time... it offers a lot of really interesting play / counterplay and general strategy. HOWEVER, This game's progression is designed in a way where it feels like it does not want you to play it. The hard lock progress barriers are SO ANNOYING. And so obvious too. Its the main thing that makes this game hard to come back to. The first time you play, you will maybe beat the first boss? Unlikely, but even if you do you definitely wont have the cards or HP left to get very far in the next stage, and most definitely not have good enough cards to do enough damage. And who designed this path choice system? choose from one of three routes at the beginning... then keep going on that path until the boss? Why even bother? And, once again, the game pretty much forces you to just always choose the path of least resistance, because the risk reward for fighting enemies is never worth it. Lose a bunch of your hard to recover health for some gold and a card? When I can just choose the route that gives me a bunch of free cards and gold with no fights? Lol. And back to the forced progression. What prompted me to leave the review is that, on my third go, I was doing really well, and scraped by after defeating mr tesla. It was a good fight, and I was ready to go after that and maybe die to the boss man. BUT NO. the game said, uh, your ARBITRARY score is 200 points too low to even keep playing... ????????? What the hell?????? who would do that? why would I fight tesla, if I was just going to lose anyways? like seriously... Game shoots itself in the foot tremendously every step of the way, but the core mechanics are fun enough to balance that out. So just treat it more like a linear arcade game rather than an intelligent roguelite/like and its a lot less frustrating. But yeah... the score was ridiculous. extremely stupid mechanic. Especially since there is no indication of this score anywhere until you get there. Why not give me a chance to up my score before fighting, especially if its 200 points off? (it was 11,701 / 11,900 points to proceed). Ridiculous.

It's a shame that this wonderful game didn't get more attention. This great indie game has a really good and entertaining story to offer. I backed it on Kickstarter back then and wasn't disappointed. For me, it's one of the best card games of recent years.

It's a fun puzzle game that's unique. On the wokeness scale the character randomizer is very bad. You'll get female names with male voices and character models. Update: After 5 hours I had a run that was doing well enough to progress but because I hadn't unlocked all 52 story cutscenes I can't progress unless I grind a bunch of more runs. This artificial increase in game length plus the mismatched voices of the characters is enough for me to change my review to a negative. The core game is fun but I feel like I've already seen it all and instead of letting me win, the game wants me to do chores first.
